findings.obligation: P7 and E15: GET /admin/instance/integrations/secrets-key/start-over is answered only while the stored secrets key cannot be opened and no running replica opens it, and in all other conditions the user does not get that page; with P6: the page offers Replace while the key opens and Start over only while it does not.
findings.observation: Every occurrence of the start over address in the oracle (feature lines 1217, 1245, 1264, 1286, 1303) sits in state I-26 or I-31. No scenario opens that address while the stored secrets key opens, and no scenario asserts that a page in that state offers no way to start over. An implementation that registers the GET without the key-mode guard - the very Impact the design records, the GET of the start-over door is registered behind the same guard - passes all six scenarios while showing a healthy Foundry the discard-everything confirm to anyone with a stale link, which is the highest-cost wrong behaviour this value can produce. The repository already owns this law for the sibling door at feature line 250, a generate request changes nothing where generating does not apply, so this is a missing row and not a missing capability.
findings.remediation: Add the missing state to the S2 oracle in that same door-does-not-apply pattern: with the instance key set and the secrets key opening, Priya opens the start over address, is answered this Foundry integrations page with the stored secrets key and the Activity as they were, is offered Replace secrets key and is offered no way to start over. One scenario, reusing the existing steps.

findings.obligation: The S2 Expected: in every run the reading doors leave the stored key, every credential, the activity list and the config version untouched. Falsifier: a start-over GET that writes a row, an activity line or a version bump.
findings.observation: The as-they-were step reads only the stored secrets key through the seam and the whole Activity list. Nothing reads the config version, so a reading door that bumps the version and makes every replica rebuild is invisible to the oracle. In state I-26 the key half is additionally narrowed: stored_secrets_key returns None whenever the held instance key does not open the row, so None equals None holds for any write that leaves the row unopenable. The dangerous write is still caught, since a key sealed under the current instance key reads Some, and scenarios 1 and 6 add a restore-and-verify that observes the original key and credential surviving, so this is a narrowing of the declared observation rather than its absence.
findings.remediation: Read the stored config version in remember and compare it in then_nothing_replaced - the store already exposes config_version, which the reload reads - or have DESIGN move the version half of the Expected to the store or handler verification that owns it and say so in the row disposition.

findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/instance_integration_setup.rs:2941 TICKS, used at :3094 in given_other_server_opens_key and :3129 in given_a_minute_passes
findings.obligation: The oracle observes the live-replica gate, so the second server beat must be in the database before the admin reads the page; determinism of the scenario and the feedback-loop budget.
findings.observation: After each clock advance the step waits a fixed 1200 ms of real time for the running servers to tick, while the spawn step just above it polls the second server own page under LIVE_BOUND for the same kind of fact. At the lane reload of 200 ms that is about six ticks of headroom and it held in the cited run, but it is a load-sensitive wait on a machine whose known failure mode is replica-boot timing under concurrency, and a missed beat presents as the live-server sentence simply being absent - indistinguishable from the missing behaviour this scenario is RED for.
findings.remediation: Wait on the observable state instead: poll, bounded by LIVE_BOUND as the spawn step already does, until the second server integration_replica_states row carries a beat_at at the advanced clock reading, and only then let the When proceed.

diagnostic: Rejected at the DISTILL S2 oracle phase, before craft, on one concrete closure defect. The six new scenarios are constructible, drive only the production router, read business observations with teaching failure messages, and carry a measured semantic RED of 8 failing cases - 3 on the absent offer and sentence with the shipped I-26 words intact, 5 on the start-over door answering 404 - with no scaffolding failure; the minute-passes construction and the stopped-server gate are feasible and discriminate a stale beat from a fresh one, and the S1 rows still hold after the step move. What blocks is finding 1: P7 and E15 promise that the start-over confirm is answered only where the stored key cannot be opened, and the oracle observes no case in the state where the key opens, so an unguarded GET - the design own Impact wording - passes every scenario while offering a healthy Foundry the discard-everything confirm. One scenario in the shipped door-does-not-apply pattern closes it. Findings 2 and 4 are non-blocking oracle work (the config-version half of the declared preservation, and a fixed real-time wait where a bounded poll on the beat row is available), finding 3 is a design copy inconsistency under I-31 that the oracle leaves unpinned and that must be settled before the promise is claimed complete. Re-review only the added state and finding 1, retaining the judgments above.
